messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testRenderWrappedTextWordCut()` tests wrapping behavior on the string "Thisisatest." with a very narrow width of 7 characters. The test expects the line break after "Thisisa" (7 chars) and then "test.". The current bug report identifies a bug in the method `HelpFormatter.findWrapPos(String text, int width, int startPos)`.

Examining the code snippet of `findWrapPos` reveals that it attempts to find a wrap position in the text. The first part of the method tries to find a newline or tab character before or at the width limit (lines 907-910) and returns that position plus one if found. If no newline or tab is found and the wrap position goes beyond the length of the text, it returns -1 as no wrapping is needed (lines 912-914).

The method then tries to locate the last whitespace before the wrap limit (lines 923-927) and if found returns it. Otherwise, it attempts to find the next whitespace after the wrap limit by incrementing position while the character at position is not a space or newline or carriage return (lines 936-941).

However, the while loop in lines 937-941 checks loop condition `(pos <= text.length()) && ...` and uses `text.charAt(pos)`. This means if `pos == text.length()`, `text.charAt(pos)` will throw a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` because valid character positions are `0` to `text.length() - 1`. The correct condition should be `(pos < text.length())` to avoid calling charAt with an index equal to text length.

Thus, this off-by-one error in the loop condition causes `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when there is no whitespace after the wrap width and we try to increment pos until it hits text.length(). The test "Thisisatest." has no spaces so it triggers this edge case.

Summary: The root cause is the while loop condition on line 937 in `HelpFormatter.findWrapPos` uses `pos <= text.length()` instead of `pos < text.length()`, leading to an out-of-bounds exception when calling `charAt(pos)`.

This matches the failure and the detailed issue report indicating this exact line problem.

No other recent bug reports are present, so this diagnosis is based on the bug report and code snippet analysis.

Next steps would be to fix the condition in `findWrapPos` to prevent the exception.
